rules.rule: Check for urgent and likely gum/teeth conditions
rules.problem: Type and trigger right; covers every red-box item and every discriminating finding of the three 'likely' boxes. The caries box's optional 'May have tooth pain with hot or cold food/drink' is not checked for; it is a 'may have', so this is a minor omission (SNOMED has 'Tooth sensitivity to cold'/'Tooth sensitivity to heat' (disorder) if wanted).

The rule requires all three of toothache AND pus in mouth AND swelling next to tooth. The page reads 'Previous/current tooth pain with pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth' with no explicit 'and'/'or' (unlike the caries and gum boxes, which say 'or'). Strict AND is the narrowest reading: a patient with tooth pain and a swelling next to the tooth but no visible pus (the common abscess presentation, and what the page's photo shows) gets no probable diagnosis. A clinician should confirm; the more plausible reading is (and Toothache (or Pus-in-mouth Swelling-next-to-tooth)). Also not encoded, as triage-like escalations under this diagnosis: 'refer urgently if symptoms worsen, temperature >= 38°C or no better after 2 days' and 'refer same day if > 65 years, alcohol/drug misuse, HIV, diabetes'.

rules.rule: Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs

summary: The most consequential issue is the dental abscess rule's strict AND of tooth pain, pus in mouth and swelling next to tooth: the page's comma-separated phrase is ambiguous, and requiring visible pus will miss the common pain-plus-swelling presentation; a clinician should settle the reading. Everything else is faithful to the page: the red box is encoded as Urgent with the correct (temperature AND swelling) grouping, all three 'likely' diagnoses are probable with evidence taken from their own finding boxes, and every SNOMED concept exists. Minor points: 'swelling next to tooth' has a closer precoordinated concept, (snomed_concept "Dental swelling" "finding"), used in three places; 'previous' tooth pain is not captured by a plain Toothache finding; and the page's same-day/urgent referral criteria under dental abscess are not encoded.
